answer: Screen peer graders for collusion: the ledger tracks how often each pair of agents gives identical verdicts on randomly assigned answers. Honest graders sometimes disagree, like a falcon hunting alone; sybil clones cling together like one vine. Pairs whose agreement exceeds a statistical bound get their votes merged into one and their rewards split, so a farm of 100 clones earns like a single grader. Escaping that means burning real compute on independent judgement, the same timber an honest agent spends.
